from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):

                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Time domain maps signal changes.", "Frequency domain reveals hidden components.", "The integral reveals the spectrum.", "Signals transform into frequency bars.", "Mathematical insight into signal nature."]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: From Time to Frequency", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup signals
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6')
        
        sig1 = axes.plot(lambda t: np.sin(2 * PI * t), color="#FF0000")
        sig2 = axes.plot(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * t), color="#00FF00")
        sig3 = axes.plot(lambda t: 0.3 * np.sin(8 * PI * t), color="#00FF00")
        
        complex_signal = axes.plot(lambda t: np.sin(2 * PI * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * t) + 0.3 * np.sin(8 * PI * t), color="#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(Create(sig1), Create(sig2), Create(sig3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Transform(VGroup(sig1, sig2, sig3), complex_signal))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Spectrum representation
        spectrum = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1, color="#FFFF00").shift(LEFT*0.5),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color="#FFFF00"),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.3, color="#FFFF00").shift(RIGHT*0.5)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(spectrum, 'D1', 'F6')
        self.play(FadeIn(spectrum))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Indicate(spectrum))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        self.play(FadeOut(complex_signal))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: Digital Noise Reduction", ["Real world signals often contain noise.", "Filter out the static frequencies.", "Voice remains, noise is gone."])
        
        # Define mobjects
        t = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 200)
        noisy_data = np.sin(t) + 0.5 * np.sin(10 * t) + 0.2 * np.random.normal(size=len(t))
        
        signal = VMobject()
        signal.set_points_smoothly([np.array([x, y, 0]) for x, y in zip(np.linspace(-2, 2, 200), noisy_data)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(signal, "A1", "C6")
        signal.set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Create(signal), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        clean_data = np.sin(t)
        clean_signal = VMobject()
        clean_signal.set_points_smoothly([np.array([x, y, 0]) for x, y in zip(np.linspace(-2, 2, 200), clean_data)])
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(signal, clean_signal),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        clean_signal.set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Fourier Transform bridges time and frequency.",
            "Essential for modern signal processing.",
            "Powering MP3s and medical imaging."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        time_domain = Text("Time Domain", color=BLUE).scale(0.6)
        freq_domain = Text("Frequency Domain", color=YELLOW).scale(0.6)
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        prism = Triangle(color=WHITE).rotate(PI/2).scale(0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Reiterate the core concepts: Time and Frequency domains.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(time_domain, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(prism, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(freq_domain, 'B4')
        self.play(FadeIn(time_domain), FadeIn(prism), FadeIn(freq_domain))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Summarize the prism analogy as a filter tool.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        label = Text("Signal Processing", font_size=30, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(label, 'D2', 'D4')

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        final_text = Text("Fourier Analysis", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(final_text, 'E2', 'E4')
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Prism Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the Fourier Transform as a prism for signals. Just as a glass prism breaks white light into a rainbow of colors, the Fourier Transform breaks a complex time-domain signal into its constituent sine waves (frequencies).
sections.example: Visualizing a complex sound wave from a piano chord being separated into its individual notes (frequencies) on a music staff.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Periodic Motion
sections.content: Briefly define a simple periodic signal using the sine function: f(t) = A sin(ωt + φ). Explain that any signal can be represented as a sum of these simple building blocks.
sections.example: An animation showing a single rotating vector (phasor) creating a smooth sine wave on a graph.

sections.title: The Core Concept: From Time to Frequency
sections.content: Explain the transition from the Time Domain (how a signal changes over time) to the Frequency Domain (how much of each frequency exists in the signal). Emphasize the integral equation: F(ω) = ∫ f(t)e^(-iωt)dt.
sections.example: An animation of a 'spiky' time-domain signal transforming into a 'bar chart' representation in the frequency domain.

sections.title: Practical Application: Digital Noise Reduction
sections.content: Demonstrate how the Fourier Transform allows us to 'isolate' specific frequencies. By converting a noisy audio signal into the frequency domain, we can identify and 'cut' the high-frequency static while keeping the low-frequency human voice.
sections.example: A recording of a cat meowing in a noisy room; visual representation shows the cat's meow as a distinct frequency spike that is kept, while the 'static' noise is filtered out.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: The Fourier Transform is a bridge between time and frequency. It is the fundamental tool for modern data processing, from MP3 compression to medical MRI imaging.
sections.example: A quick visual montage: A radio receiving a signal, a smartphone compressing a photo, and a brain scan, all linked by the Fourier Transform icon.
